content:
Fake Mass reports are basically killing X and many other platforms right now.

With new AI tools and AI agent tools, the volume of fake mass reports has increased dramatically, and it's one of the tools that political activist groups use to silence people critical of their movement. Currently, platforms like Discord, Facebook, X, and Instagram experience hundreds of millions of reports per hour. 

A lot of my mutals have been permanently banned on X for disagreeing with certain groups of people, and their appeals have fallen on deaf ears. Instead of engaging in a fair market of ideas, they resort to using automated tools or groups of actual human users to target a person with egregious TOS violations. 

A lot of other times, mass reports limit your account's reach, causing shadow bans, ghost bans, where only a small number of people see your posts. 

This also causes a chilling effect, as you don't know which group you offend is going to cause them to do a mass report attack on you. 

I know this is a VERY COMPLEX problem to solve. None of the major platforms has been able to effectively manage this issue, and it's causing massive issues pretty much everywhere right now. 

But I think if X implements better tools like semantic cross-referencing to assess whether the report matches the content violation will help with mitigating some of these problems. If the content assessed by "grok," for example, does not violate TOS and contradicts the report, then the reports should be ignored. 

It should include circuit breakers so that mass reports of established accounts do not lead to automatic suspension and are then prioritised for human review. 

Reporting accounts should also have reputational weighing, where if they routinely engage in reports with minimal platform engagements, the weight of the report should be very low. Whereas a long-standing user with a high reputation making a report should have a stronger signal.

content:
AI x Prediction Market, protocols

On prediction markets, humans mostly trade narratives. Machines optimize probabilities.

An autonomous agent doesn’t care about vibes, charisma, CT narratives, or CNBC storytelling.

They are probabilistic by nature. They score confidence, update beliefs, optimize expected value, run continuously, and don’t get tired from checking 50 related markets at once.

Prediction markets are basically RL-friendly markets in the wild.

The venues themselves are becoming reinforcement learning environments.

- clear reward functions.
- continuous feedback.
- objective outcomes.
- always-on repricing.

→ perfect sandbox for autonomous systems.

Another thing is x402 is probably one of the biggest unlocks for autonomous finance infra in years. Agents can now buy probabilities about future states.

Agent asks for data → server requests payment → agent pays USDC → API returns forecast/inference/execution.

The stack for this meta is already forming.

- @Polymarket : real-time machine-readable probabilities on politics, macro, sports, geopolitics, crypto, regulation, AI itself. 

– @HeyElsaAI : one of the clearest examples of x402 turning into real execution infrastructure. Agents can already route, simulate, rebalance, and execute onchain actions autonomously through multi-agent coordination rails.

I'm convinced that AI and crypto are perfect for each other in many ways

- verifiable compute 
- verifiable training
- AI resistent sybil defence (proof of humanity etc)
- agent payments & micropayments
- decentralized training & GPU markets

So I went down the rabbit hole to see how I could

- train a model in a decentralized way
- while still keeping some weights private
- and zk proving that it was trained humanely/ethically 

That last one ran into a whole lot of problems and led me down an even deeper rabbit hole until I arrived at mechanistic interpretability

From the outside, AI weights do not appear to correspond to how they act in any meaningful way

Mechanistic interpretability (mech interp) is about opening up neural networks and discovering why the weights do what they do

It basically says "don't just trust the black box of AI" which reminds me a lot of the philosophy of crypto

Anyway, Claude and I wrote a curriculum mainly for myself to help me understand mech interp. Thought I'd open it up for other software engineers

If you can't read AI papers or PyTorch but would like to, this is for you. It walks through 6 interpretability papers and replicates them in PyTorch. You can run them directly in the browser (using my huggingface space)

New research from Microsoft Research

I see a lot of AI engineers handwriting agent skill docs and hope they generalize.

It treats the skill doc as a trainable external state of a frozen agent instead.

It introduces SkillOpt, where an optimizer model makes validation-gated edits to the skill file. It adds, deletes, or replaces instructions, with a textual learning rate that controls how aggressively each round rewrites the doc. The agent itself never changes.

On GPT-5.5 it adds 23.5 points in direct chat, 24.8 with Codex, and 19.1 with Claude Code over no skill. It beats human-written skills, TextGrad, GEPA, and EvoSkill, carries zero extra inference-time cost, and the learned skills transfer across models and harnesses.

connect to open router → see exact costs per model per task → use GPT 5.5 for tool calls → use open source for lightweight tasks → route the right model to the right job → watch your margins double →

みなさま　おはようございます✨❣

「Claude CodeとCodex、どちらを使えばいいのか」

この問いを持っている方は多いと思います。
結論から言うと、2026年の正解は「どちらか一方」ではありません。
ただし、両者の役割は根本的に異なります。

まずCodexとは何か。
一言で言うと「OpenAIが作った、コードを書くことに特化したAIアシスタント」です。
ChatGPTの兄弟で、文章で指示するだけでコードを書いたり、バグを直したりしてくれる。
非常に優秀なコーディング専門家です。

しかしCodexには、できないことがあります。

AIエージェントそのものを設計・構築すること。
複数のエージェントを束ねて管理・監督すること。これはCodexの領域ではありません。

それを担うのがClaude Codeです。
Claude Codeは、AIエージェントを一から設計し、構築し、複数のエージェントを並列稼働させながらその監督までを自律的にこなします。
2026年Q1からはクラウド上での24時間稼働も可能になり、PCを閉じて眠っている間も動き続けます。

数字で見るとその差も明確です。
コード生成速度ではClaude Codeが5分で約1,200行を生成するのに対し、Codexは10分で約200行。
品質面では、盲検レビューでClaude Codeのコードが67%の確率で高評価を得るのに対し、Codexは25%にとどまります。
一方でトークン消費量はClaude Codeがはるかに多く、同等のタスクでCodexの2〜3倍のコストがかかります。

だからこそ、賢い使い方はこうなります。

**シンプルなエージェントを大量に作る場合のみ、**Codexに部品コードを安く書かせ、そのコードをClaude Codeに渡してエージェントとして組み立て・稼働させる。コストを大幅に削減できます。

一方、高度・複雑・緻密性が要求されるプロジェクトにはCodexを挟んではいけません。
粗悪な部品が混入すれば後で必ず副作用が出ます。
そういった案件はClaude Code一択です。

料理に例えるなら、Claude Codeは「キッチン全体を設計し、スタッフを指揮し、レストランを経営するオーナーシェフ」。
Codexは「シンプルな料理を大量に仕込む時だけ頼む、コスト効率の良い仕入れ先」。

用途を誤らなければ、組み合わせることで最強になります。

Claude Code ＝ エージェントを作り・動かし・束ねるオーナーシェフ
Codex ＝ シンプル案件限定で投入するコスト削減の切り札

この使い分けを知っている人が、2026年の開発現場で最も賢く戦える。

title: 「Claude Mythos」が1万件以上の脆弱性を発見　しかし修正追い付かず　Anthropicが報告書
content: 米Anthropicは5月22日（現地時間）、セキュリティプロジェクト「Project Glasswing」の初期報告を公開した。約50社のパートナー企業が1カ月で高・重大レベルの脆弱性を1万件超発見した成果に加え、同社が独自に進めてきたオープンソースソフトウェアのスキャン結果も公表された。
